items.name: Chanel
clues: Paris, 1910, starting with a small shop that sold hats.
A perfume from 1921 that is still one of the most famous in the world, and a quilted handbag named after a month in 1955.
Black and white, tweed jackets, pearls and the little black dress.
Marilyn Monroe once said that the only thing she wore in bed was a few drops of its perfume.
Karl Lagerfeld, the designer from Hamburg, ran its fashion from 1983 until he died in 2019.
Named after its founder, whose nickname was Coco.

items.name: Tiffany & Co.
clues: New York, 1837.
Diamond engagement rings. In 1886 it introduced a ring with six thin metal claws that lift the diamond up towards the light.
A special shade of light blue, on every box and every bag.
At the start of a 1961 film, Audrey Hepburn eats breakfast on the pavement while she looks into its shop window.
The founder's son, Louis Comfort, became famous for colourful glass lamps.
The founder's surname, plus “& Co.”

items.name: Rimowa
clues: Cologne, 1898.
Something almost every traveller owns, made from a light metal that was also used to build early aeroplanes.
Shiny silver metal with parallel grooves.
In 2016 it built replicas of an early all-metal aeroplane, the Junkers F 13.
Owners say the dents it collects at airports over the years are part of the charm.
Six letters, usually written in capitals, starting with RIM.

items.name: Montblanc
clues: Hamburg, 1906.
A pen called the Meisterstück, German for “masterpiece”, first made in 1924.
Black and gold, with a small white six-pointed star on top, meant to look like a snowy mountain peak.
Its most famous pen is about a hundred years old and still looks almost the same.
The number 4810 is engraved on its nibs: roughly the height, in metres, of the highest mountain in the Alps.
The French name of that mountain, written as one word.

items.name: Moncler
clues: 1952, in a mountain village near Grenoble, in France.
Quilted jackets filled with down, first made for mountaineers and skiers.
Shiny and puffy, with a little round badge on the sleeve.
In 1954 its jackets went up K2 with the Italian expedition that was the first to reach the top.
An Italian businessman, Remo Ruffini, bought it in 2003 and turned it into a fashion brand based in Milan.
A short form of Monestier-de-Clermont, the village where it started.

items.name: Versace
clues: Milan, 1978.
Bold, glamorous clothes with bright prints and gold baroque patterns.
Gold and black, and a logo of a woman from Greek myth with snakes for hair.
In 2000 Jennifer Lopez wore its green jungle-print dress to the Grammys. So many people searched for photos of it that Google decided to create Google Images.
After its founder died in 1997, his sister Donatella became its creative director.
The founder's surname: Gianni ___.
